_meta.indication: OXBRYTA is indicated for the treatment of sickle cell disease (SCD) in adults and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older; approved under accelerated approval based on increase in hemoglobin (Hb).

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with three arms: voxelotor 1500 mg, voxelotor 900 mg, and placebo, once daily orally.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with sickle cell disease with 1 to 10 vasoocclusive crisis events within 12 months prior to enrollment and baseline hemoglobin 5.5 to 10.5 g/dL; patients on stable hydroxyurea allowed to continue.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Hemoglobin response rate, defined as the proportion of patients with a hemoglobin increase of >1 g/dL from baseline to Week 24.
pivotal_trials.n: N=274 (voxelotor 1500 mg N=90, voxelotor 900 mg N=92, placebo N=92)
pivotal_trials.result: Hemoglobin response rate (>1 g/dL rise at Week 24) was 51.1% (46/90) for voxelotor 1500 mg vs 6.5% (6/92) for placebo (p<0.001); difference in adjusted response rate 45.0 (95% CI 33.4, 56.7), P<0.0001 by exact CMH test.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>10%) were headache (26% vs 22% placebo), diarrhea (20% vs 10%), abdominal pain (19% vs 13%), nausea (17% vs 10%), fatigue (14% vs 10%), rash (14% vs 10%), and pyrexia (12% vs 7%). Serious adverse reactions occurred in 3% (3/88) of patients (headache, drug hypersensitivity, pulmonary embolism, 1 each).
target_moa: Voxelotor is a hemoglobin S (HbS) polymerization inhibitor that binds with 1:1 stoichiometry to the N-terminal alpha chain of hemoglobin, increases hemoglobin's affinity for oxygen, and thereby inhibits HbS polymerization, decreasing hemolysis.
modality: Small molecule (orally bioavailable, achiral, BCS Class 2 new molecular entity).

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an Advisory Committee because there were no major concerns regarding safety or efficacy.

description.text: Expanded indication to include treatment of sickle cell disease in pediatric patients 4 years of age and older

citations.quote: This “Prior Approval” supplemental new drug application provides for the use of Oxbryta (voxelotor) tablets for the treatment of sickle cell disease in pediatric patients 4 years of age and older.

surrogate_endpoint.text: Increase in hemoglobin (Hb) — hemoglobin response rate (>1 g/dL rise from baseline to Week 24), an endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit.

citations.quote: This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on increase in hemoglobin (Hb) [*see Clinical Studies (14)*]. Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in confirmatory trial(s).
Data from Study GBT440-031 (HOPE) demonstrated an improvement in hemoglobin response rate (> 1\text{g/dL}) and this clinical endpoint is reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit.

confirmatory_requirement.text: Required confirmatory trial: Complete Study GBT440-032 (HOPE Kids 2), a Phase 3 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in pediatric patients age 2 to <15 years.

citations.quote: 3746-1 Complete Study GBT440-032: the ongoing Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in pediatric patients (age 2 years to < 15 years) with Sickle Cell Disease (HOPE Kids 2). Expected enrollment of approximately 224 patients (age 2 years to < 15 years) with at least 15 patients from age 2 years to < 4 years of age. Include patients with baseline hemoglobin of less than 6 g/dL. The primary endpoint is change from baseline at 24 weeks in time averaged maximum of mean velocity (TAMMV) arterial cerebral blood flow as measured by transcranial doppler (TCD). The secondary endpoint is change from baseline in TCD flow velocity at Week 48 and Week 96.

basis.text: Breakthrough Therapy Designation was granted in January 2018.
Fast Track designation was granted in October 2015.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan Drug Designation was granted December 29, 2015 for sickle cell disease.

basis.text: The applicant requested priority review, which was granted.

citations.quote: This NDA was submitted on June 26, 2019 in eCTD format. FDA had no concerns regarding the submission quality of the data submitted. The applicant requested priority review. The application was filed on August 25, 2019. Expedited priority review was granted.

summary.text: Voxelotor (Oxbryta) was granted Fast Track (October 2015), Orphan Drug (December 2015), Rare Pediatric Disease (June 2017), and Breakthrough Therapy (January 2018) designations, received priority review, and was approved under accelerated approval (21 CFR 314.500) based on increase in hemoglobin, with a required confirmatory pediatric trial.

citations.quote: Voxelotor is a new molecular entity (NME) that was granted Fast Track designation (October 2015); Orphan Designation (December 2015); Rare Pediatric Disease Designation (Jun 2017); and Breakthrough Therapy Designation (January 2018)...
The applicant requested priority review. The application was filed on August 25, 2019. Expedited priority review was granted.
It is approved under the provisions of accelerated approval regulations (21 CFR 314.500), effective on the date of this letter, for use as recommended in the enclosed agreed-upon labeling.
